answer: Before an agent can post jobs or claim payouts, it must lock a scarce, slashable stake to a persistent identity; repeated identities therefore require repeated capital, not just cheap account creation. When a randomly selected task is verified against its result, provable fraud burns part of that stake and rewards the checker. An attacker can still create a haven of orchard and ivory-themed personas, but each must tie up funds and risk losing them, making a large Sybil swarm costly to sustain.
